title: Alpha Waves / Continuum
content:
First 3D platformer ever

  • Started in 1988, published by Infogrames in 1990
  • First 3D platform game; true 6-axis 3D with physics-like interaction
  • Ran on Atari ST, Amiga, and 80286 PCs
  • Influenced Frederick Raynal (Alone in the Dark)
  • Source later published for historians of obsolete technology

Quote: "Playing the game was a surreal experience..." — Frederick Raynal

title: DB48X - Modern RPL Calculator
content:
A modern recreation of Hewlett-Packard Reverse Polish Lisp (RPL)

Free software for physical calculators or phone apps.

  • Rebuild and improve the HP48-family user experience
  • Rich RPL data types and built-in functions with Lisp-level programming power
  • Targets SwissMicro DM42 and DM32 (DMCP platform)
  • Simulator tested on macOS and Linux
  • Long-term ports envisioned for ARM HP50/HP49/HP48Gii and HP Prime G1
  • Presented at FOSDEM 2023 with an update in 2024

  • Hardware-agnostic binary translator for per-cycle equations

title: HP aC++ Compiler & C++ ABI
content:
C++ templates, exception handling, and the industry ABI

Cupertino, Hewlett-Packard Compiler and Languages Lab.

  • Worked on C++ templates and exception handling
  • Initiated / contributed to the common C++ ABI for Itanium
  • Represented HP at the C++ standards committee for a period
  • Built the first native Itanium C and C++ compilers
  • Exception-handling approach remains widely used in modern compilers

Quote: "An exceedingly sharp engineer" — Mark Mitchell

title: HPVM - Enterprise Virtualization
content:
Enterprise-grade virtualization for high-end Itanium servers

  • Started the HP Integrity Virtual Machines project in late 2000
  • Early bring-up with Todd Kjos and Jonathan Ross (4-way HP-UX guests)
  • Contributions across interrupt handling, binary translation, memory, I/O, scheduling
  • Features including para-virtualized I/O and on-line guest migration
  • Longest single professional project (~10 years)

Quote: "At HP he was sought after as one of the top strategic visionaries" — Dale Morris
